subject: Security review: PII flow, role mapping, and transfer clarifications
messages:
From: Dana Schultz <dana.schultz@healthtech.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: security@healthtech.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SSQ: PII handling, role mapping, KMS & cross-border transfers

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking this on. We're running a security questionnaire for our vendor review and have a couple of focussed clarifications about how Redwood handles PII and cross-border transfers. Questions are short — a consolidated spreadsheet is attached (healthtech_ssq_v2.xlsx). Would you be able to confirm the answers below or point us to the right artifacts?

Top items we need clarified before next Tuesday's procurement sync:
- Primary data classification for user-generated content we send to your API (PII / pseudonymized / other).
- KMS key custody model: Customer-managed keys (CMK) supported? If yes, which clouds/regions?
- Subprocessor geography: Do any subprocessors process data in APAC or India specifically (we need country-level names)?
- Audit logs & retention: what events are retained, for how long, and how are they exported for our auditors?
- Data flow diagram that shows ingestion -> inference -> cache/kv retention -> logs. Any redaction rules applied to logs?

Please reply with short answers and any artifacts you can share (redacted diagrams, subprocessor list, SOC2 scope note). If easier, a single PDF with answers is fine.

Thanks,
Dana Schultz
Senior Security Manager
HealthTech Inc.

Attachments: healthtech_ssq_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Schultz <dana.schultz@healthtech.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SSQ: PII handling, role mapping, KMS & cross-border transfers

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide a consolidated response and a redacted dataflow diagram. I'm attaching a draft PDF that maps short answers to the spreadsheet rows (redwood-ssq-draft.pdf).

High-level answers up front:
- Primary classification: user-generated text is treated as Customer Data; depending on your classification it will typically fall under PII if it contains identifiers. We can mark fields for tokenization/pseudonymization on ingest where feasible.
- KMS: We support customer-managed keys (Bring Your Own Key) in AWS (KMS) and GCP (Cloud KMS) for Private deployments and Dedicated offerings. Hosted API customers can use our KMS for hosted keys; we offer key-wrapping integration for Enterprise contracts.
- Subprocessors: I've pulled the latest list; Ben will confirm country-level processing details for each subprocessor.
- Audit logs & retention: Request/response metadata, routing, and error/tracing events retained by default 30 days for hosted plans; extended retention options for Enterprise/Dedicated. We can export logs to your S3/GCS/Syslog for audit review.
- Diagram: attached an internal redacted SVG (converted to PNG) showing the approximate flow (redwood-dataflow-v1.png).

I'm looping in Ben (product infra) for the KMS/subprocessor specifics and Marcus (security) for logging retention and export artifacts. We'll follow up with the SOC2 scope note and the per-country processor map.

Best,
Sofia
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-ssq-draft.pdf (pdf); redwood-dataflow-v1.png (diagram)

Hi all — quick technical clarifications to add to the draft:

1) KMS and key custody
- Hosted API: we manage the envelope keys by default; we provide key-wrapping so enterprises can bring a root key (BYOK) via AWS KMS/GCP KMS. This provides cryptographic separation for stored model artifacts and cold snapshots.
- Dedicated/Private: full CMK support (customer uploads key material to customer KMS and we integrate via key-wrapping).
- Regions: BYOK is supported in us-east-1, eu-west-1, and asia-southeast1 for Dedicated installs.

2) Data classification & tokenization
- We can configure ingestion pipelines that perform deterministic tokenization or PII redaction by regular-expression-based transforms. Those are optional and part of onboarding config; by default we do not apply customer-specific PII redaction.

3) Subprocessor locations & per-country notes
- Short list attached: subprocessor-list-20270521.csv (contains processing-country column). Most subprocessors process in US and EU; a subset (inference optimization vendor) routes some telemetry to a partner in India — this is only telemetry and not customer payloads; we'll confirm and redact per your sensitivity.

4) Logging & retention exports
- We retain request metadata and error traces 30 days by default. For Enterprise contracts we can extend to 1 year and provide S3/GCS export hooks. Access to raw request/response bodies is limited and requires an access request + justification and is logged in our audit trail.

I'll attach the subprocessors CSV and a short export config snippet. Sofia / Marcus: please add any security policy language and SOC2 references.

Thanks,
Ben
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — quick follow-ups from procurement/security:
- Can you explicitly confirm whether any subprocessor in India has access to plaintext customer payloads (user inputs/responses)? If not, please confirm whether telemetry-only processing is documented and isolated.
- For the BYOK regions you listed, do any of the cloud-regions support export restrictions that would be relevant to EU data subjects? We need an explicit statement for our DPA annex.
- For logs: are there redaction masks applied to request/response bodies in logs by default? If not, what is the recommended configuration to avoid storing PII in logs?

Also, could you attach the SOC2 Type II scope page (redacted if needed) so our auditors can see the in-scope systems? A Drive link or an auditor artifact is fine.

Appreciate the speed — procurement deadline is next Wed.

Dana

Hi Dana — summary and artifacts attached. Answers inline below and in the attached PDF (redwood-ssq-final.pdf).

1) Subprocessors in India & payload access
- Confirmed: no subprocessor in India has access to plaintext customer payloads. The vendor that performs telemetry/optimization routing to India only receives aggregated telemetry (metrics, anonymized call stats) — we documented this in the attached CSV under processing_country and access_scope columns. We will provide a redacted attestation for proof upon contract execution.

2) BYOK regions and EU data subjects
- BYOK is supported in eu-west-1 (Ireland) and us-east-1. For EU data subjects we recommend eu-west-1; the export control model follows the cloud provider export rules. For Private Dedicated installs, EU customer data can be fully isolated in eu-west-1 and we will include a data transfer annex in the DPA.

3) Log redaction
- By default hosted logs do not redact request/response bodies. We recommend enabling the ingestion transform pipeline (deterministic tokenization or regex redaction) during onboarding if you want PII removed from logs. For Enterprise we can enable automatic redaction hooks and choose retention windows. All accesses to raw payload exports require an internal access request; those actions are audited.

4) SOC2 artifact and evidence
- Attached: SOC2-scope-redacted.pdf (redacted scope). For auditors we can provide a signed attestation and a scoped read-only artifact link.

Attachments in this email: redwood-ssq-final.pdf (pdf) — consolidated answers mapped to your spreadsheet; SOC2-scope-redacted.pdf (pdf); subprocessor-list-20270521.csv (csv); redwood-dataflow-v1.png (diagram).

Next steps:
- We'll send the final DPA annex language and the per-country subprocessor attestations by Monday.
- If you want a quick call to walk through the diagram, happy to set 30 minutes next week.

Best,
